notes.summary: Raw geometric envelopes are LSC; positivity is equivalent to continuity. Graded primary ideals give a factorial formula, and insertion proves actual decreasing-net closure.
notes.detailedSummary: On every excellent reduced primary section, finite continuous raw C/D envelopes agree and are nonexpansive. A greatest or maximal D minorant exists exactly when the raw envelope is continuous, equivalently its USC regularization is positive. The factorial formula does not recognize an increasing limit as D. Strict insertion constructs one decreasing C-net before any energy argument. All supports, full qualified G331 restrictions and exact primary-gauge rules remain.
notes.text:
Use only the entire qualified G331. Work on the reduction of an excellent local ring and X={v:v(a)=1}, retaining every prime support. G331 supplies the independently geometric core, its continuous uniform closure C, and actual decreasing-C-net completion D. Core positivity means actual negative effective real Cartier presentations on actual primary blowups with nonnegative degree on every contracted integral curve. No envelope theorem is imported.

For finite continuous f put p(f)=sup{h in D:h<=f}. Large negative constants are competitors, so p is finite and bounded. If h=inf h_alpha, the increasing open sets {h_alpha<f+epsilon} cover X. Compactness and directedness select one index valid everywhere. Then h_alpha-epsilon is a C competitor at least h-epsilon. Thus the C and D suprema coincide; p is LSC and below min(f,0).

If p is continuous, finitely many C competitors, combined by maximum, approximate it uniformly from below. Closedness gives p in C. Conversely p in D is USC, hence continuous. Its upper regularization p* remains below min(f,0); if p* belongs to D, it is a competitor, so p*=p. Therefore positivity of p*, continuity of p, and existence of a greatest D minorant are equivalent. Any maximal minorant is greatest because maximum with every competitor remains admissible. Negative shifts give ||p(f)-p(g)||<=||f-g||.

Define J_k={r:v(r)>=-k f(v) for every v in X}. Valuation axioms make J_k an ideal. If f>=-M, it contains a^ceil(kM), hence is unit or primary. It is integrally closed: a violated inequality and a monic ideal-integrality equation, after quotienting by the support, produce a unique least-valued leading term, impossible in a valued field. J_k J_l subset J_(k+l), so -v(J_(j!))/j! increases. Rational single-ideal profiles are dense in C. Approximate a C competitor and subtract a small rational primary constant. If -v(I)/k<=f, then I subset J_k; sufficiently divisible factorial profiles dominate it. Consequently p(f)=sup_j[-v(J_(j!))/j!] on all supports. This identity alone gives no increasing-D closure.

Actual decreasing-D closure is proved independently. On a normal branch, let u=inf_i u_i for a decreasing D-net. If u vanishes anywhere, G331's zero dichotomy makes every u_i identically zero. Otherwise a tail has upper bound -c<0. For continuous F>u, compact strict-test covers select one u_i<F everywhere, then one term g of its actual C-net satisfying g<F and g<-c/2. Choose 0<b<1 with b||g||<min(F-g). Then q=(1-b)g belongs to C and u<q<F, including at bottom points.

Insertion into the continuous minimum of two strict C majorants makes their family downward directed. Its infimum is u: upper semicontinuity and a Urysohn cutoff construct, for any x and finite t>u(x), a continuous F>u with F(x)<t; insertion supplies q(x)<t. Reverse pointwise order is therefore ONE decreasing C-net. For reduced nonnormal rings apply this branchwise on finite normalization and use qualified full-fibre D descent. This proves decreasing closure, not arbitrary-infimum or increasing closure.

Signed primary differences are uniformly dense. Their rational lattice formula is min(v(I)-v(J),v(K)-v(H))=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH). The uniform closure is a real vector lattice containing constants and separating all supports through min(v(t),N)=v((t)+a^N). Compact lattice approximation gives every continuous function.

For another primary gauge b, d(v)=v(b) and 1/d are bounded positive continuous. T(v)=v/d(v) transports obstacles and functions by f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v). Order, raw envelopes, regularization and the J_k inequalities obey this exact one-factor cocycle. Nilpotents are invisible; dimension zero has the unique empty envelope. No compact-global result is asserted for nonprimary partial sections.

Complete proof and artifacts: n1.md, whole-proof.md, P12.3-paper.md and native-notes.json. Execution establishes consistency, not mathematical correctness.

notes.summary: Global continuous geometric envelopes on every excellent normal surface, with arbitrary residue field and characteristic.
notes.detailedSummary: Current Stacks condition (4), normal completions and the full connected fibre yield regular common models. A residue-weighted intersection matrix constructs an actual ample exceptional boundary; global sections and the integral punctured graph identify an actual primary blowup. Actual Cartier pushdown and a greatest finite nef vector dominate every D competitor. Signed density gives all-continuous CE. No higher-dimensional pushdown or arbitrary-model cofinality is inferred.
notes.text:
Use qualified G331 and n1. Let R be excellent normal local of dimension two, with arbitrary field and positive, zero or mixed characteristic. Normalize the product blowup of finitely many prescribed primary ideals, including a. This integral projective surface is identical on the puncture, has finitely many singular points, and their completions are normal by current Stacks 0C23. These verify precisely condition (4) of current 54.14.5, 0BGJ/0BGP. Its complete immediate (4)->(3) proof gives a regular projective common model T, identical on the puncture and principalizing the collection. Complete-ring resolution, rational-singularity and gluing foundations are disclosed published dependencies.

Full Stacks 0AY8 gives Gamma(T,O)=R and the full geometrically connected closed fibre. Write a O_T=O(-sum b_i E_i), b_i positive integers. Regular factoriality makes every fibre curve E_i actual Cartier. This Cartier cut has pure codimension one, so its support is the whole fibre.

Let M_ij=deg_k O(E_j)|E_i, retaining actual residue degrees. Off-diagonal intersections are nonnegative local lengths times residue degrees; M is symmetric and its graph connected. Pullback of the ample tautological bundle gives Mb<=0, with a strict coordinate. Indeed Bl_a has a fibre curve: otherwise its proper birational morphism is finite and an isomorphism over normal R, making the primary ideal principal, contrary to the height theorem in dimension two.

Set A=-M and t_i=b_i z_i. Direct expansion yields t^T A t=sum_i(Ab)_i b_i z_i^2+sum_(i<j)(-A_ij)b_i b_j(z_i-z_j)^2. This is positive definite: equality forces z constant on the connected graph and zero at a strict coordinate. Every principal A_J is positive definite with nonpositive off-diagonal entries. Its inverse is entrywise nonnegative. For A_J x=y>=0, write x=x_+-x_-; a nonzero negative part would give x_-^T y=x_-^T A_J x_+-x_-^T A_J x_-<0. Also A^-1 1 is strictly positive, since a zero coordinate would have nonpositive row product. Clear denominators to obtain integers d_i>0 with Md<0.

The actual divisor E=sum d_i E_i has O(-E) positive on every fibre curve. Complete Stacks 0B5Y proves ampleness on the full possibly nonreduced fibre over any field; 0D2N gives relative ampleness near the closed point, hence throughout the local base. Serre generation supplies a high power L^q giving a closed immersion. I=Gamma(T,L^q) is an actual coherent ideal in R, proper and unit off m, hence primary, with I O_T=L^q. Include immersion sections among its generators. T and Bl_I are integral closed subschemes of the same projective space with the identical dense punctured graph, hence identical. Thus T is an ACTUAL primary blowup. The argument also applies to regular common refinements.

Before interpreting envelopes by ideals, prove Cartier pushdown. For a regular common primary refinement mu:T'->T and negative effective real curve-nef D', set D=mu_*D'. On regular T this is actual negative Cartier. For every E_i, effective pullback and supported cycle projection give D.E_i=D'.mu^*E_i>=0, with actual residue degrees. Let F=D'-mu^*D. On the mu-exceptional curves M_J f>=0; the inverse sign forces f<=0. Hence F is actually negative and h_(D')<=h_D on every support. This is a surface argument, not a higher-dimensional analogue.

Evaluation first uses Frac(R/support(v)) and a proper centre. Exceptional equations are nonzero on its generic puncture, hence have finite values. Put nu_i=ord_Ei/b_i. Trace coefficients of h are c_i=b_i h(nu_i), and sum b_i v(E_i)=1. Uniform core approximation gives c_i<=0, Mc>=0 and h<=sum c_i v(E_i). Finite coefficient errors are bounded by max_i |delta c_i|/b_i. For bounded D use its actual decreasing C-net and finite trace limits. Any D competitor under f>=-B can first be clamped to max(h,-B).

For a signed primary obstacle determined on T, f(v)=sum b_i f(nu_i)v(E_i). The compact polytope -B b_i<=c_i<=min(0,b_i f(nu_i)), Mc>=0 contains -B b. It is closed under coordinatewise maximum: in row i select the vector giving the maximum ith coordinate; its diagonal is unchanged and every other contribution increases. The maximum of coordinate maximizers is a greatest feasible c*. Its actual negative real nef Cartier evaluation H* lies below f. Pushdown and clamping show EVERY D competitor, on EVERY primary model, lies below H*. Thus p(f)=H*. Signed density and nonexpansivity prove p(f) in C for every finite continuous obstacle.

This proves CE on all excellent normal surfaces, every primary gauge and every support. No arbitrary-proper-model cofinality or resolution above dimension two is claimed. Full Keeler/G331 real-perturbation qualifications persist. Complete artifacts: n2.md, whole-proof.md and source-application-ledger.md. Rerun python finite_diagnostics.py; python build_delivery.py; python final_audit.py. Finite matrix checks are diagnostic, not this theorem's proof.

notes.summary: Isolated characteristic-zero CE; general normal characteristic-zero envelopes are continuous on the finite-Q open locus, with the infinite-Q stratum unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: The three-author published BdFF source is reconstructed using only geometric C to source-nef, fixed base trace zero and finite determining vertices. Integral 4.11 applies after denominator clearing in the isolated case. General 3.17 gives coherent graded section ideals, possibly nonprimary multiplier ideals and primary lower-error truncations. Inequalities extend first on O={v(d(K)Jac)<infinity}, never by divisorial density within a closed K_L. Global infinite-Q positivity remains open. Uniform correction values are bounded on all points or all centred divisors iff the ideal is unit/primary.
notes.text:
Use qualified G331 and n1. Here R is a normal algebraic germ at a CLOSED point over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension at least two. The applied source is the THREE-author Boucksom–de Fernex–Favre, Duke 161 (2012). Complete immediate numerical, envelope, general multiplier and isolated approximation units were read; Hironaka, numerical, singular-multiplier/Takagi and Izumi foundations are disclosed dependencies.

A geometric core divisor is source-nef by its contracted-curve degrees. Uniform core approximation of g in C gives coefficient convergence, with fixed base trace ZERO since the marked point has codimension at least two. Source 1.12(a) converts this to numerical convergence; closedness gives a source-nef H_g. Only core/C->source-nef is used. No source-nef->D recognition or dense-set extension of a merely USC inequality is assumed.

For f=(v(A)-v(B))/N take a normal common primary model Y. The Cartier obstacle C=(Z(B)-Z(A))/N evaluates to f, where Z(I)=-ord(I). Let E_i be its exceptional primes, b_i=ord_Ei(a)>0 and nu_i=ord_Ei/b_i. Cartier order bounds give MZ(a)<=C. Source 2.11–2.13 and 2.15–2.17 yield the largest source-nef trace envelope W=Env_pi(C_Y), with MZ(a)<=W<=C and W<=0 at base trace zero. If W=0, continuity/density imply f>=0 on the entire section, so p(f)=0.

For an isolated singularity, CLEAR denominators first: C0=NC is integral and W0=NW. Integral 4.11 gives actual coherent multiplier ideals b_k with Z(b_k)>=kW0+Z(d(K))+Z(Jac), and Z(b_k)/k->W0 coefficientwise. Correction ideals are unit or primary, not necessarily strictly primary. Their combined divisor is at least c Z(m). Source 4.7–4.9 gives W0<=epsilon Z(m)<0. Therefore Z(b_k)>=(k+c')W0. Rounding c' UP preserves the inequality because W0 is negative. Put B_k=Z(b_k)/(N(k+c')). Then B_k>=W and B_k->W. A nonzero W makes b_k proper eventually; discard a finite unit prefix. Hartogs puts the sections in R, and primary powers make the retained ideals actual primary. The zero case uses the unit ideal.

Let eta_k=max_i((B_k(E_i)-C(E_i))^+/b_i)->0. Largest-trace comparison gives B_k+eta_k Z(a)<=W, hence B_k-eta_k<=W<=B_k on normalized divisors. The continuous primary profiles are uniformly Cauchy there, hence on the WHOLE section by divisorial density. Their limit U is in C and below f. For EVERY D competitor h<=f, select ONE term g of its actual C-net with g(nu_i)<=f(nu_i)+epsilon at every finite determining vertex. H_g+epsilon Z(a) has constrained trace, so g-epsilon<=W on divisors and, by continuity, <=U everywhere. Since h<=g, h<=U+epsilon. Thus U=p(f). Signed density and nonexpansivity prove global CE in this exact isolated characteristic-zero setting.

For the GENERAL nonisolated case use 3.17, not isolated 4.11. Let Q=d(K)Jac be coherent nonzero, O={v(Q)<infinity} OPEN and K_L={v(Q)<=L} compact. The omitted closed stratum consists of supports containing Q. Canonical Cartier shifts do not alter d(K).

Set a_m=pi_*O_Y(mC0). Proper coherence and normal Hartogs make these actual ideals in R. Cartier order gives a^(M1 m) subset a_m; each is unit/primary and the sequence is graded. No graded finite generation is asserted. Its source coefficient limit is W0. General 3.17 with b_k=J(a_bullet^k) yields Z(b_k)>=kW0+Z(Jac)+Z(d_bullet(K)), and coefficient convergence. Since d(K)^m subset d(mK), Z(d_bullet(K))>=Z(d(K)), so Z(b_k)>=kW0+Z(Q). These multiplier ideals may be NONPRIMARY.

Choose A0>M0 with W0>=M0 Z(a), and put b'_k=b_k+a^(A0 k), U_k=Z(b'_k)/(Nk). These are actual unit/primary ideals. The second maximum term is strictly below the limiting coefficient at each centred divisor, so U_k->W, while U_k>=W+Z(Q)/(Nk). Finite trace errors eta_k=max_i((U_k(E_i)-C(E_i))^+/b_i) tend to zero; largest-trace comparison gives U_k+eta_k Z(a)<=W. Thus their continuous profiles satisfy W-v(Q)/(Nk)<=u_k<=W+eta_k on normalized divisors. The functions g_k=u_k-eta_k are global C competitors below f, by continuous divisorial density.

Subtracting the estimates gives u_k-u_l<=eta_k+v(Q)/(Nl) and the reverse inequality. FIRST extend these continuous inequalities on OPEN O by density there; only afterwards restrict to K_L. Divisorial density inside K_L is not presumed. They give local uniform convergence on bounded-Q neighbourhoods to continuous U on O, with 0<=U-g_k<=eta_k+v(Q)/(Nk). Thus U<=p(f) there. For every D competitor the same ONE finite-vertex continuous term gives g-epsilon<=W=U on divisors, extending continuously on O. Hence p(f)=U on O. Signed density and global nonexpansivity extend this to every finite continuous f. Since O is open, p*=p there. Global continuity/positivity at infinite-Q supports remains unproved unless another proved sector applies.

The uniform correction criterion is exact: for nonzero ideal I on an excellent normal positive-dimensional local domain, v(I) is bounded on ALL points, equivalently on ALL centred divisors, iff I is unit or primary. The primary direction follows from a^N subset I. If proper nonprimary I subset p<m, the positive-dimensional excellent quotient R/p has a boundary point killing I. Each nonempty open {v(I)>L} contains a centred divisor by density. A fixed finite divisor list cannot replace this global criterion.

For R=k[x,y,z,t]/(xy-z^2) at the origin, in EVERY characteristic, normality follows from the hypersurface domain, S2 and codimension-one regularity. The Jacobian (x,y,2z) has radical (x,y,z), quotient k[t]; the t-order support kills it. The canonical defect is unit. Thus Q is nonprimary and unbounded. A failed correction estimate is not a CE counterexample; n5 gives an independent actual-cover CE proof in characteristic zero.

Complete artifacts: n3.md, whole-proof.md and the private full-literal source ledger. Rerun python extract_literal.py; python capture_source_units.py; python build_delivery.py; python final_audit.py. Source applications and the mathematical arguments, not execution, support these claims.

notes.summary: Exact smooth BFJ envelopes and extended USC/decreasing-net theory, constructed only after global CE.
notes.detailedSummary: At smooth affine CLOSED algebraically closed characteristic-zero germs, substantive closed-face 3.11 and entire 3.18/3.22 estimates pass through every retraction, giving actual primary uniform approximation on all semivaluations. After global CE, continuous obstacle majorants yield one decreasing C-net for extended USC obstacles. Arbitrary decreasing USC nets are stable by the proved decreasing-D closure. Local finite-Q continuity alone does not supply this global conclusion.
notes.text:
Use qualified G331 and n1–n3. The smooth application is ONLY a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension at least two. G331 already grants the full BFJ class specialization on every semivaluation, with global bottom adjoined. DVR and empty cases are direct.

The actual BFJ setting, all-support retractions 1.11–1.14, extension 2.7–2.8, substantive closed-simplex 3.11 and the ENTIRE 3.18 proof including 3.22 were checked. Closed-face continuity uses multiplier profiles with error A/k and thinness bounded on the fixed closed simplex. Interior convexity does not prove boundary continuity. Extension is the infimum over EVERY retraction.

A signed primary obstacle is determined on a simple modification's dual complex. For its BFJ nef envelope W, write W_j=j^-1 Z(L_infinity(jW)). In the nonzero case, reindexing 3.18 gives W_j<=W<=(j/(j+C0))W_j on divisors. The profiles are actual primary for sufficiently large indices; unit and zero are handled separately. If -M<=W, then 0<=W-W_j<=MC0/j. Closed-simplex continuity extends the inequality on every face; taking all-retraction infima preserves the SAME uniform bound on every semivaluation. Contract completed primary ideals exactly by G331. The uniform limit is in C and dominates every D competitor by the full granted specialization. Signed density and nonexpansivity give CE. No global thinness bound is used.

Now suppose a normal section has GLOBAL CE. For an extended USC obstacle phi, clip by zero. It is bounded above and may have poles. The finite continuous nonpositive majorants F are downward directed by minimum and have infimum phi. At x and finite t>phi(x), upper semicontinuity and a Urysohn cutoff give a continuous majorant whose value at x is below t; this also works at a pole. If t>0, zero already suffices.

Each P(F) lies in C by CE. Ordered by decreasing F, these form ONE actual decreasing C-net. Its infimum u is in D by definition, lies below phi, and dominates every D competitor below phi. Thus u is the greatest geometric minorant P(phi). The bottom obstacle is obtained directly by decreasing negative constants. This construction follows CE and does not exchange unproved arbitrary suprema and infima.

If phi_i decreases as an arbitrary USC net to phi, its envelopes decrease. Their infimum belongs to D by n1's proved decreasing-D closure and lies below phi; maximality forces it to equal P(phi). The positive bounded gauge cocycle transports the result exactly. These extended results require GLOBAL CE; n3's finite-Q open-locus result does not establish them on the omitted support stratum.

For a smooth DVR the normalized boundary is a singleton, actual Cartier point divisors give all nonpositive slopes, and P(phi)=min(phi,0). Dimension zero is empty. No singular or positive-characteristic SNC transfer or unconditional pole normalization formula is claimed.

notes.summary: Actual dominating finite CE covers and the exact full-conductor positive domain for finite continuous obstacles.
notes.detailedSummary: For finite reduced covers of a normal target, every minimal source component must dominate. Full-support normal-closure orbit maxima preserve C/D, including inseparable and nonminimal supports, and transfer CE from an actual source. Primary conductor masks give finite-locus raw equality. With source CE, regularization is the full-fibre maximum of source envelopes and is positive exactly when they are fibre constant. Without source CE the criterion is raw-source continuity plus fibre constancy. No universal cover or unconditional pole formula is claimed.
notes.text:
Use qualified G331 and n1–n4. Let A be excellent normal local and B a finite reduced algebra containing A, with EVERY minimal source component dominating A. Retain all semilocal centres and support primes. Qualified G331 supplies full-fibre positive C/D descent and full-support finite normal-target traces, with their quotient-field and inseparable qualifications.

Fibre maximum M(h)(v)=max_(rho(w)=v)h(w) preserves C and D. On a source domain component normalize, take a normal closure of its function-field extension, and the finite integral closure E over A. G331's actual coefficient trace is q sum_(g in G)delta_(gw), with support the FULL fibre, so that fibre is the finite orbit of a lift, including inseparable multiplicity. Finite maxima of automorphic pullbacks are in C, fibre constant and descend positively. Across dominating components take another finite maximum. Finite fibre maximum commutes with an actual decreasing C-net: all finitely many lifts eventually satisfy any strict finite test, and directedness supplies one index. This proves D preservation, including bottom.

For a base continuous f, source competitors descend by fibre maxima and base competitors pull back. Hence p_B(rho^*f)=rho^*p_A(f). If the ACTUAL source has CE, compact surjective quotient topology gives CE downstairs. No theorem provides such a cover universally. Gauge factors are shared by each fibre.

An actual cover is A=k[U,V,W]/(UW-V^2), B=k[s,t], U=s^2,V=st,W=t^2, localized at the origins. The base is normal in every characteristic. This finite extension has generic degree two, inseparable in characteristic two; its closed fibre has basis 1,s,t and length three, so it is not flat of rank two. Polynomial extensions preserve the cover. Over algebraically closed characteristic zero the actual source is smooth in n4's exact range, so all these targets have CE, including the nonisolated examples with extra variables. Characteristic-two higher-dimensional extensions receive no unsupported smooth CE conclusion.

For general excellent reduced R, let S be finite normalization, c its conductor and rho the full compact quotient. Fibres are singleton at finite conductor value and precisely conductor-quotient fibres at infinity. The finite-conductor locus is OPEN and dense upstairs: each normal component sees a nonzero conductor and its divisorial points are dense. The infinity stratum remains CLOSED.

For continuous f>=-B, clipped by zero, and source C competitor g, define PRIMARY masks b_N(v)=-(B/N)v(c+a^N). They belong to C, equal -B on the whole infinite-conductor stratum, and tend to zero at finite conductor values. The source function max(g+rho^*b_N,-B) lies below rho^*f, equals -B on that whole stratum and is full-fibre constant. Positive descent gives downstairs competitors. Taking suprema proves rho^*p_R(f)=p_S(rho^*f) at finite-conductor points, with <= everywhere.

If EVERY actual normal centre has CE, U=P_S(rho^*f) is continuous. Its dense agreement with rho^*p_R makes the latter's upstairs upper regularization U. For bounded F on a compact quotient, F*(v)=max_(rho(w)=v)(rho^*F)*(w): cover the compact fibre by controlling neighbourhoods and use closedness of rho for one base neighbourhood; the reverse inequality follows by testing each lift against every base neighbourhood. Therefore p_R(f)*(v)=max_(rho(w)=v)U(w).

Positivity is equivalent to U being constant on EVERY full fibre. Sufficiency is qualified positive C descent. Necessity follows from n1: positive regularization equals continuous raw p_R; its pullback and U agree densely, hence everywhere. This is also equivalent to continuity of the displayed fibre maximum and existence of a maximal D minorant. The positive domain is closed under uniform limits.

Without source CE, the exact criterion is still: p_R* is positive iff the RAW source envelope is continuous and full-fibre constant. If p_R is continuous, its pullback is a source competitor. Dense finite-conductor equality and LSC of the raw source envelope force equality everywhere. Conversely continuous fibre-constant source envelopes descend positively.

For USC obstacles with poles, the universally valid normalization description is the supremum over source D competitors below the pulled obstacle and constant on EVERY fibre. G331 proves that description by descent. The unconstrained maximum formula was proved only for finite CONTINUOUS obstacles. All finite formulas obey the exact one-factor gauge cocycle. No unconditional pole formula or whole P12.6 theorem is inferred.

notes.summary: Actual nonnormal failure of maximal minorants; complete geometric excellent-curve envelopes equal ideal clipping.
notes.detailedSummary: The double plane with maximal gauge and obstacle -1-1/v(y) has an explicit discontinuous raw envelope whose regularization violates a normal-branch inequality. Thus no maximal D minorant exists. On every excellent reduced curve, actual Cartier slopes and full positive descent give every nonpositive branch vector and P(phi)=min(phi,0), including extended obstacles and exact gauge/residue weights. Literal analytic/CLD radial compatibility remains distinct.
notes.text:
Use qualified G331/B341/E350 and n1,n5. This counterexample is explicitly NONNORMAL. Let R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), a=m, in any characteristic. Its normalization comprises planes A=R/(y), B=R/(x); conductor descent identifies exactly their boundary points q killing the nonshared parameter and assigning z value one. Set f(v)=-1-1/v(y), with reciprocal infinity zero. Since v(y)>=1, f is continuous, finite and strictly negative in [-2,-1]. It equals -1 on A and takes -2 at B's ord_m.

Every B function h in D satisfies h(v)<=h(ord_m): v(I)>=ord_m(I) for primary profiles, then pass to uniform C limits and one decreasing net. Thus every B competitor is <=-2, attained by the constant -2.

On A take J_n=(x^n,xz^(n-1),z^(2n)). For a0=v(x), b0=v(z), min(a0,b0)=1, its profile j_n is -1 when a0<=b0, and -min(1+(a0-1)/n,2) otherwise, including -2 when a0=infinity. The tuple (j_n,-2 on B) is in normalization C and compatible at q, hence descends positively to a downstairs competitor. It increases to -1 on A except q, remaining -2 at q and on B. The upper bounds above prove this is exactly p_R(f).

Monomial valuations a0=L,b0=1 tend to q, so raw p_R is not USC. Its regularization has value -1 at q but -2 at B's ord_m, violating the universal B inequality. Therefore p_R* is not in D, and n1 proves there is no maximal D minorant. This is an actual ring, gauge, obstacle and detectable failure, not a normal counterexample or a failed estimate.

For every excellent reduced local CURVE, finite normalization has finitely many local DVR branches q above m, not merely irreducible components. A centred DVR semivaluation has zero support and is a positive multiple of ord_q, so its primary section is ord_q/a_q, a_q=ord_q(a)>0. A regular conductor element has finite value on every branch; normalization fibres are singleton. Actual effective Cartier point divisors, with the contracted-curve condition empty, give every finite nonpositive slope by real scaling. Full positive G331 C descent gives all finite nonpositive branch vectors downstairs. The single sequence max(u,-j) supplies every extended nonpositive vector in D. This geometric construction precedes ideal clipping.

Hence for ANY branch obstacle, including positive infinity and poles, P(phi)(q)=min(phi(q),0). The finite discrete link makes it automatically USC, continuous for finite obstacles. It agrees exactly with the complete ideal-psh envelope. Gauge change multiplies the branch value by a_q/b_q. Qualified B341/E350 give reference weights [kappa(q):kappa(m)]a_q, including inseparability; a branch bottom has positive reference mass and infinite curve energy.

Literal radial extensions remain different. On two normalized analytic discs, (-1,0) forces nodal value at least zero from the zero branch by USC. On the negative radial branch, a nonnegative interior maximum contradicts its subharmonic maximum principle with zero outer boundary. The dossier's CLD counterpart is retained only at its stated disc/conductor hypotheses; no fresh general CLD comparison is claimed.

Use qualified G331/B341/E350 and n1. On surfaces B=F>=0 and E(u)=-F(u,u)/2. E350 retains actual-primary-model, reduced-boundary, all-support, specified-limit and finite-reference-moment qualifications. It grants no increasing-D recognition.

In k[x,y]_(x,y), maximal gauge, I_j=(x,y^j) and u_j=-v(I_j)/j increase to zero except at the support-(x) point q, where the limit is -1. Monomial valuations v_L(x)=L,v_L(y)=1 tend to q. The limit is non-USC and outside D; its regularization zero is geometric, so this does not refute normal CE.

For ALL r,s>=0, the staircase threshold of m^r I_j^s at x-exponent a<r+s is r+s-a+(j-1)max(0,s-a). Summation gives length R/(m^r I_j^s)=r(r+1)/2+rs+j s(s+1)/2. Consequently e(m,I_j)=1, e(I_j)=j, F(u_j,u_j)=1/j, E(u_j)=-1/(2j), and measure mass is 1/j. For EVERY capacity input -1<=phi<=0 in D, order gives F(phi,phi)<=1 and conditional Cauchy gives F(u_j,phi)<=1/sqrt(j). Pairing and Markov yield Cap{-u_j>epsilon}<=1/(epsilon sqrt(j)). Energy, mass and capacity convergence do not make the exact increasing limit geometric.

On R=k[X,Y,Z]_(X,Y,Z)/(XY-Z^2), all characteristics, put a0=v(X),b0=v(Y). Then min(a0,b0)=1 and v(Z)=(a0+b0)/2 when finite. For I_n=(X^n,XY^(n-1),Y^(2n)), u_n=-v(I_n)/n is -1 when a0<=b0, otherwise -min(1+(a0-1)/n,2). It increases to h=-1 off q with support (X,Z), h(q)=-2. Monomial a0=L,b0=1 tends to q. Thus h is outside D while h*=-1 is geometric.

The actual m-blowup is regular: the X chart has Z=Xz',Y=Xz'^2, the Y chart is analogous, and the Z chart has x'y'=1. Its exceptional conic has degree two over every field, giving reference measure 2 delta_(ord_m). Let z_j=-v((X)+m^j)=-min(v(X),j). This is an actual decreasing C sequence, hence z=-v(X) belongs to D, without assuming finite energy. For EVERY admissible phi, F(z_j,phi)<=F(z_j,-1)=2. Bounded pairing and ordinary SEQUENTIAL Borel MCT imply integral v(X)dmu(phi)<=2. Therefore Cap{a0>T}<=2/T and Cap{q}=0. For 0<epsilon<1, the approximation error set is {a0>1+n epsilon}; for epsilon>=1 it is empty. The non-D limit is a capacity limit and continuous outside open sets of arbitrarily small capacity.

The exact universal parity formula is length R/I_n^k=(n^2+n)k^2+(n^2-n+2)k. Identify R with k[s^2,st,t^2]. Pair columns of s-exponent 2p and 2p+1, 0<=p<nk. Their even t-threshold maximizes 4n i+(2n+2)j subject to i,j>=0, i+j<=k, ni+j<=p. For p<k the maximizer is i=0,j=p. For n>1 and p>=k, put i0=floor((p-k)/(n-1)) and q=p-k-(n-1)i0. Below i0 the slot constraint binds and the objective increases; above it the exponent constraint binds and the objective decreases. The next candidate differs by 4n-(2n+2)(n-q)<=-4, so the maximizer is i0,k-i0. Each even/odd column pair contributes its even threshold. The first range sums to (3n-1)k^2+(n+1)k, the remaining blocks to (n-1)^2k(k+1), yielding the formula. For n=1 only the first range occurs.

Thus e(I_n)=2n^2+2n, F(u_n,u_n)=2+2/n and E(u_n)=-1-1/n. Counting semigroup degree below 2k gives length R/m^k=k^2 and e(m)=2. These are universal counting arguments with explicit signs.

Own finite diagnostics PASS on 392 smooth staircase cases, j=1..8,r,s=0..6, and 64 parity cases, n,k=1..8. They additionally check 142 chain matrices, 1828 principal inverses, 71030 quadratic vectors and 357 finite maximum pairs on recorded boxes. They prove only those exhaustive finite results, not the universal theorems.

notes.summary: New perfect-characteristic-p theorem: Cartier obstacles on an ACTUAL smooth primary model have uniform actual geometric approximation on all supports.
notes.detailedSummary: Assume a perfect characteristic-p field, normal integral affine finite-type B, closed x of codimension at least two, and an actual smooth primary blowup Y=Bl_J, identical off x and principalizing the gauge. Coherent unit/primary section ideals, all-index Fekete and the normal height-one criterion give the raw envelope. Complete GJKM Section 4 and corrected Keeler generation produce actual primary profiles g_m with 0<=p(f_C)-g_m<=c v(J)/m<=cN/m everywhere. This proves geometric positivity and continuity. Universal model existence, Cartier K_B, Jacobian/energy premises and increasing-D recognition are not used.
notes.text:
Use qualified G331 and n1. Let k be PERFECT of characteristic p>0, B normal integral affine finite-type over k, x CLOSED of codimension n>=2, and a a proper x-primary gauge. Assume an ACTUAL primary blowup Y=Bl_J B is smooth over k, identical off x and principalizes a; J is x-primary. Put A=J O_Y=O(-F_J), ample and globally generated, and H=-F_J. Fix an integral fibre-supported Cartier divisor C, without a sign assumption. No universal existence of Y is asserted.

For every support FIRST use Frac(B/support(v)) and its valuation ring. Its generic point is on the puncture, where Y is the identity. Properness gives a centre. The generically trivial lattice O(C) has a nonzero quotient-field generator, and f_C is minus its value. Cartier order bounds by the principalized primary divisor make all evaluations finite and bounded; G331 gives continuity. No map from Frac(B) to a nonminimal-support quotient is presumed.

Set I_m=Gamma(Y,O(mC)), m>=1. Proper coherence makes it finite. Sections are regular at every codimension-one point of B because C is supported over codimension-at-least-two x; normal Hartogs puts them in B. Hence I_m is an actual ideal, unit off x. For a fixed integer M with C>=-M E_a, it contains a^(Mm), so is nonzero unit/primary. The section family is graded; no graded finite generation is claimed.

The finite nonnegative values v(I_m) are subadditive. ALL-index Fekete gives s(v)=lim_m[-v(I_m)/m]=sup_m[-v(I_m)/m]. These profiles are actual C competitors below f_C. Conversely -v(L)/r<=f_C implies, at every fibre prime divisor of NORMAL Y, ord_E(L)>=-r coeff_E(C). At other prime divisors C is zero and L is regular. The height-one criterion for invertible fractional ideals gives L O_Y subset O(rC), hence L subset I_r. Rational profile density with a small negative shift, then n1's C/D equality, prove p(f_C)=s on the ENTIRE section. Fekete alone does not prove positivity.

On smooth Y define the actual graded base ideals b_m=I_m O_Y tensor O(-mC), unit off the fibre, and t_m=tau(b_bullet^m). The ENTIRE GJKM arXiv:1712.00980v3 Section 4, 4.1–4.6 and immediate proof, together with Mustata's entire Section 3, gives b_m subset tau(b_m) subset t_m and t_(ml) subset t_m^l. Coherence, BMS subadditivity and Frobenius-trace foundations are disclosed published dependencies.

Apply GJKM 4.6 with D=C,E=mC,lambda=m,d=n+1. A nonzero I_r supplies a section of rC; H is ample globally generated and E-lambda D=0 is nef. Y is smooth integral over PERFECT k and projective over finite-type AFFINE B, precisely the source's hypotheses. Thus O(K_Y+mC+dH)t_m is generated for EVERY m. K_Y is ON Y; K_B need not be Cartier.

Ordinary Serre generation supplies ONE fixed c>=0 such that A^c O(-K_Y-dH) is generated. Tensoring gives F_m=O(mC)t_m A^c globally generated for ALL m. J_m=Gamma(Y,F_m) is an actual coherent ideal in B by the same Hartogs argument. The inclusion b_m subset t_m gives I_m J^c subset J_m, so it is unit/primary. Generation yields the ACTUAL fractional-ideal equality J_m O_Y=O(mC)t_m A^c, not merely numerical equality.

Pull this equality to every support quotient centre. Values of t_m are finite because it contains b_m, unit on the generic puncture. A finite global generating set has a unit coefficient at the valued centre. Therefore g_m(v)=-v(J_m)/m=f_C(v)-(c/m)v(J)-(1/m)v(t_m). Both losses are nonnegative. Thus g_m is an ACTUAL continuous geometric profile below f_C on ALL supports.

For fixed m and every l, b_(ml) subset t_(ml) subset t_m^l implies -v(I_(ml))/(ml)=f_C-v(b_(ml))/(ml)<=f_C-v(t_m)/m=g_m+(c/m)v(J). The all-index Fekete limit is unchanged along multiples ml. Letting l tend to infinity gives p(f_C)<=g_m+c v(J)/m. Since g_m is a competitor,

0<=p(f_C)-g_m<=c v(J)/m<=cN/m,

where a^N subset J. The error is uniform on the FULL primary section, including nonminimal supports. Hence p(f_C) belongs to C, is finite continuous, equals its USC regularization and is the greatest D minorant.

Source precision is essential. Mustata 1109.3825v2 Section 3 allows PERFECT k, but Section 4.1 is projective over ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED k and alone cannot prove affine-base generation. GJKM 4.6 is the exact extension. Its complete immediate proof uses Frobenius trace, projection formula, Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity and corrected Keeler 1.5. The complete Keeler statement/immediate proof and ENTIRE v5 erratum were read. False old 3.3 is not used; E1.3 employs finite faithfully flat altered base, and E2.4/E2.5 repair the argument and retain 1.5. Deeper BMS, trace, regularity, alteration/EGA, Fujita/Serre, Hartogs and coherence foundations are disclosed, not recursively freshly certified.

Use qualified G331 and n1,n2,n4,n8. Define (SM) for a normal closed algebraic germ over PERFECT characteristic p: EVERY finite collection of primary ideals, including its gauge, admits after affine shrinking an ACTUAL smooth common PRIMARY blowup, identical off the marked point and principalizing the collection. One model carrying one obstacle is insufficient.

Under SM, a signed rational obstacle f=(v(A)-v(B))/r is determined on the actual common smooth model. The integral exceptional Cartier C=Z(B)-Z(A) evaluates to r f. N8 gives p(r f) in C; positive homogeneity gives p(f)=p(r f)/r. Signed-profile density on the ENTIRE compact section and nonexpansivity extend this by uniform convergence to every finite continuous obstacle. Closedness of C proves actual positivity and continuity. N1 supplies gauge change; once global CE is proved, n4 supplies extended USC and arbitrary decreasing USC-net envelopes.

A constructive sufficient gate is useful. Begin with the prescribed product primary blowup. Suppose a finite sequence of ACTUAL blowups of coherent ideals with cosupport over the point, and finite normalizations, ends in smooth integral T. Each blowup has an actual effective exceptional Cartier divisor and relatively ample negative tautological bundle. The initial primary divisor supports the WHOLE fibre. Inductively tensor the new tautological bundle with a sufficiently high power of the pulled old ample bundle; complete Stacks 29.38.7–8 proves relative ampleness. Finite normalization preserves ampleness. The resulting O(-E) is ample for an actual integral effective FULL-fibre divisor E.

Normal-base Stein factorization gives Gamma(T,O)=B. A high power O(-qE) is generated and gives a closed immersion. I=Gamma(T,O(-qE)) is coherent, actual primary and unit off x, with I O_T=O(-qE). Include immersion sections among finite generators. T and Bl_I are the identical integral closure of the punctured graph of those generators, as in n2. Hence T is an ACTUAL primary blowup and retains the prescribed principalizations. An arbitrary projective resolution, alteration, small resolution or abstract modification does not supply this sequence or divisor.

An authenticated nontrivial SM regime is normal algebraic SURFACES at CLOSED points over perfect characteristic-p fields. N2 uses the complete current Stacks condition-(4) surface theorem to resolve the common product model and proves it an actual primary blowup. Regular finite-type schemes over perfect fields are smooth. Spread the local primary ideal's finite generators after clearing denominators and adjoin a sufficiently high power of the marked maximal ideal; this does not change its localization and forces global cosupport {x}. The global blowup localizes to the proved regular model. The nonsmooth locus has closed proper image avoiding x; remove it. Failure loci for the finitely many principalizations likewise have closed proper images avoiding x. One affine shrinking gives the required actual smooth common primary blowup. Thus SM holds with its FULL quantifier in this regime.

The proposed isolated THREEFOLD regime remains OPEN. Public primary search inspected Cossart–Piltant arXiv:1412.0868v2, the displayed Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.4. The resolution statement and its distinction between a locally principal ideal on the regular locus and an ideal trivial there do not supply the required primary blowup or preceding sequence. The full 320-page proof was NOT read or applied as a premise. Neither SM for those threefolds nor its failure is proved here. A smooth model identical off x forces the puncture smooth, excluding nonisolated singularities from SM as stated. Nonperfect fields, mixed characteristic, nonalgebraic excellent germs and nonclosed points remain outside n8's source scope. No models are promised there.
